Consumer Non-Cyclicals: Out of the fifteen sectors, Consumer Non‑Cyclicals fell to the bottom rank, placing 15th of 15 based on the median price change over the past month. Its median price movement lagged the overall SGX median, and only one of its ten constituents recorded a gain in the same period. The lag may stem from weaker consumer spending amid tighter credit conditions, higher input costs for packaged goods, recent regulatory scrutiny on advertising, and a slowdown in tourism‑driven demand, all of which uniquely pressure the Singapore Consumer Non‑Cyclicals market.
Consumer Cyclicals: The Consumer Cyclicals sector, comprising 84 listed companies, topped the sector ranking by placing 1 out of 15 based on median price changes over the past 30 days, and it outperformed the overall SGX median price movement in the same period. Positive momentum was seen in 27 of the companies, indicating that roughly a third of the constituents contributed to the sector’s strength. This robust performance is likely driven by a combination of factors unique to the Singapore market, such as a rebound in tourism, rising consumer confidence, higher disposable income, favourable exchange‑rate conditions, ongoing government stimulus measures, seasonal festival spending, and improved supply‑chain resilience. Together, these elements have helped lift demand for discretionary goods and services, reinforcing the sector’s leading position.
Transportation & Logistics: Ranking third out of fifteen sectors based on median price changes over the past month, the Transportation & Logistics sector showed notable strength, outpacing the broader SGX median. Despite only two of its eight constituents posting positive price moves, the sector’s median gain was enough to lift it above the market average. This performance may stem from heightened freight demand, easing port congestion, stable fuel costs, and supportive regulatory measures that have boosted logistics activity in Singapore. Additional influences such as regional trade flow shifts, e‑commerce expansion, labor market dynamics, and infrastructure investments also shape the sector’s health.
Healthcare: Out of fifteen SGX sectors, Healthcare ranked 12th based on its median price change over the past 30 days, with a median that lagged the overall market. Of the 40 listed healthcare firms, only eight posted a price gain, underscoring the sector’s breadth of weakness. The lagging median likely reflects heightened regulatory scrutiny, tighter reimbursement policies, slower biotech funding, an aging domestic patient base, and lingering post‑pandemic demand uncertainty, all of which uniquely pressure Singapore’s healthcare stocks. Consequently, the sector’s price momentum remains subdued relative to the broader index.
Properties & Real Estate: Out of the fifteen SGX sectors, Properties & Real Estate fell to 13th place, with its median price change lagging the overall market. Only nine of the fifty‑one listed property firms posted gains over the past month, underscoring the weak breadth. The sector’s underperformance may stem from a combination of tighter monetary policy, recent cooling measures on property transactions, rising construction costs, subdued foreign buyer sentiment and a glut of new supply, all of which are weighing on Singapore’s real‑estate outlook. As a result, the median price decline for the sector is deeper than the SGX‑wide median, reflecting the pressure on valuations. Investors should watch how these macro‑ and policy‑driven factors evolve.
Energy: Out of 15 SGX sectors, the Energy sector sits at 11th place, with its median price change lagging behind the overall market. Among its 23 constituents, only four posted gains over the past 30 days, underscoring the breadth of the decline. The lagging median likely reflects pressure from global oil price volatility, tighter regional emissions regulations, supply‑chain constraints on fuel imports, and accelerating renewable‑energy incentives that are reshaping investor sentiment. These Singapore‑specific dynamics have weighed on the sector’s momentum, leaving it under‑performing relative to the broader index.
Utilities: Despite only three of its thirteen constituents posting gains in the past month, the Utilities sector secured a solid sixth place out of fifteen in the median‑price‑change ranking, outpacing the overall SGX median movement. The sector’s relative strength likely reflects steady electricity demand, recent regulatory tariff revisions, accelerated renewable‑energy integration, stable fuel‑price environment, and ongoing grid‑infrastructure upgrades that have buoyed investor sentiment. With ten companies posting declines, the modest positive tail still managed to lift the median, underscoring how sector‑wide fundamentals can offset broad market weakness.
Consumer Defensive: The Consumer Defensive sector, made up of 30 companies, slipped to 9th place out of 15 in the median price‑change ranking, with its median move trailing the overall SGX median. Only eight firms posted a positive price change over the past month, indicating that the majority are under pressure. Diminished consumer confidence, elevated input costs, tighter credit conditions, heightened regulatory scrutiny on food safety, and currency fluctuations are among the factors uniquely shaping the health of the Consumer Defensive market in Singapore. These dynamics help explain why the sector’s median performance is lagging the broader market.
Financial Services: The Financial Services sector, made up of 29 listed firms, ranked fourth out of fifteen sectors for median price change over the past 30 days, outpacing the broader SGX. Eight companies posted a positive price change during the same period, underscoring a modest breadth of gains. The sector’s outperformance stems from higher interest rates that lift net interest margins and strong earnings from major banks, which together boost investor sentiment. Current market health is also shaped by regulatory reforms, the prevailing interest‑rate environment, regional banking stress, foreign capital inflows, and credit‑quality trends.
Communication Services: The Communication Services sector topped the SGX sector rankings, securing the 1st spot out of 15 based on median price changes over the past month. Its median gain outpaced the broader SGX index, even though only 4 of the 15 constituent companies posted positive price moves in the same period. Strong demand for digital connectivity, a supportive regulatory stance, accelerated broadband infrastructure upgrades, heightened advertising spend, regional tourism recovery and rising mobile data consumption are among the factors uniquely shaping the sector’s health in the Singapore market.
Basic Materials: Out of fifteen SGX sectors, Basic Materials ranked eighth based on its median price change over the past month, with a median move that lagged the overall market. Only seven of its thirty‑six constituents posted gains, meaning the majority posted declines and dragged the sector’s median lower than the SGX average. The weaker performance can be tied to a slowdown in global commodity demand, tighter export regulations, fluctuating input costs, and reduced construction activity in the region, all of which weigh heavily on Singapore‑listed miners and chemicals. With just a fifth of the companies posting positive returns, the sector’s health appears constrained relative to peers.
Infrastructures: The Infrastructures sector, comprising seven listed companies, ranked fifth out of fifteen based on its median price change over the past 30 days, outpacing the broader SGX median. Only two of the seven firms posted a positive price change in the same period, yet the sector’s overall momentum remained strong. This relative strength likely reflects renewed government infrastructure spending, easing of regulatory bottlenecks, robust regional trade activity, and favorable financing conditions, which have buoyed investor sentiment despite the limited number of individual gainers. Key market‑health drivers include fiscal stimulus for public works, shifts in zoning policy, fluctuations in construction material costs, and the prevailing interest‑rate outlook.
REIT: Out of 15 sectors, the REIT segment fell to 14th place, with its median price change lagging behind the overall SGX median over the past month. Among the 41 REITs, only six recorded gains, underscoring the breadth of the decline. The weak performance may stem from a combination of higher financing costs, tighter rental demand, recent regulatory tightening on leverage, an oversupply of new properties, and subdued foreign investor appetite. These Singapore‑specific headwinds have pressured valuations and kept the sector’s median return below the market average.
Industrials: The Industrials sector, comprising 126 listed companies, currently sits 10th out of 15 sectors in the median price‑change ranking over the past month. Its median price change trails the overall SGX median, reflecting broader weakness in the segment. Only 30 of the 126 firms posted a positive price move during the same period, underscoring the limited breadth of gains. This underperformance may stem from subdued demand for capital‑intensive equipment and higher financing costs that have squeezed profit margins. Additional pressures include global supply‑chain bottlenecks, elevated raw‑material prices, tighter monetary conditions, and a slowdown in regional infrastructure projects.
Technology: The Technology sector, comprising 58 listed companies, secured a 7th‑place ranking out of 15 based on its median price change over the past 30 days. It outperformed the broader SGX market on a median‑price basis, with 19 of its constituents posting positive returns during the same period. The stronger performance likely reflects robust demand for cloud and software services, continued government support for digital transformation, and favorable foreign‑exchange conditions. At the same time, the sector’s health is uniquely influenced by regional data‑center investment cycles, global chip‑supply constraints, regulatory shifts specific to Singapore, and currency fluctuations.
